interventions.speaker: EXPERT-EAU
interventions.who: EAU guideline specialist; speaks only from the guideline text he retrieved
interventions.body:
GUIDELINE
The EAU guidelines suggest that a PI-RADS score of 3 or higher mandates a biopsy. "a PI-RADS threshold of $\ge 3$ is used to trigger biopsy" and this applies to patients with suspected organ-confined disease.

WHAT THE EXPERTS' BIDS DO NOT SETTLE
EXPERT-STRUCTURED's suggestion of biopsy is not settled by the guideline because the guideline focuses on the PI-RADS score, not the combination of variables like DRE findings or comorbidity. EXPERT-COHORT's criterion, which matches the reading urologist in 24/24 cases, is not decisive because the guideline does not specify that the decision must be based solely on the PI-RADS score, but rather on a risk-adapted matrix.

WHAT THE DOCUMENTS MUST SETTLE
previous_notes - the prior biopsy status: None means the indication stands based on the PI-RADS score.
radiology_report - whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study: this is not specified, but the PI-RADS score is the primary driver.
psa_trend - the PSA velocity: the guideline does not explicitly state a threshold for PSA velocity that dictates biopsy in this context.
laboratory_results - the PSA density: the guideline links PSA density to risk stratification, which is a factor in the overall decision matrix.

REGISTRAR — pull these up, and answer exactly the question attached to each:
  radiology_report (get_mri_report) -> Does the mpMRI prose indicate whether the lesion is compared against an earlier study?
  psa_trend (get_psa_trend) -> Does the PSA velocity provide information that influences the decision beyond the PI-RADS score?
  previous_notes (get_previous_notes) -> Is the grade of the prior biopsy recorded (Gleason or ISUP)? How many biopsy sessions, and when was the last? Is he on a surveillance protocol, and is a confirmatory biopsy due? Is any treatment already agreed or declined?

OPEN QUESTIONS for this conference — these are what the decision hangs on:
  Q1. What is the significance of the PSA velocity (0.35 ng/mL/yr) in the context of the EAU guidelines for this decision?

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-PSA
interventions.who: Expert 2, PSA projector; the trajectory behind the headline PSA, with a conformal band
interventions.body:
Expert 2 here — the PSA projector. I read only the serial PSA the registrar opened.

TRAJECTORY: RISING (borderline). Last value 4.80 ng/mL over 5 points spanning 20 months; velocity -0.05 ng/mL per year; no meaningful doubling time.
PROJECTION at 6 months: 7.9 ng/mL, conformal 95% band 2.3-27.7.

Read the band before the point: it is wide by construction, and I only call a direction when the whole
band clears the last value. This does not vote on the biopsy — a rising PSA in a man with a known
diagnosis is the disease behaving as known — it tells the chair how fast the number is moving.

interventions.speaker: EXPERT-FUSION
interventions.who: Expert 3, Extra-Trees on panel + laboratory + MRI prose; speaks only on documents that were opened
interventions.body:
Expert 3 here — the fusion classifier. I read the panel, the mpMRI report — the laboratory panel was not opened, so that block is imputed and my band is wider for it; nothing from the previous notes or the PSA series.

SUGGESTION: BIOPSY   p(biopsy) = 0.80
  uncertainty  +/- 0.06 epistemic (95% band 0.67-0.92), of which 0.00 comes from values that had to be imputed
  reliability  HIGH ('firm' tier) — out-of-fold it was right 89% of the time over the 37 labelled cases in this tier

What moved me most across the labelled series: prior positive biopsy, no prior biopsy, free PSA < 15%, DWI restriction in the report, lesion >= 15 mm in the report, suspicious DRE. Out-of-fold AUC 0.794. I am the only expert that has read the report's wording, and I still cannot see the prior grade or the
surveillance history: those are in the notes, and the registrar has to carry them.

data.gist: Expert 3 suggests BIOPSY, p=0.80 +/- 0.06, HIGH reliability (firm, fusion_nolab)

interventions.speaker: VERIFIER
interventions.who: second EAU reader; checks against the guideline whether this can be decided yet
interventions.body:
SUFFICIENCY
The documents retrieved by the registrar—radiology_report, psa_trend, and previous_notes—directly address the questions posed by the moderator regarding the PSA velocity and prior biopsy status.

ALIGNMENT WITH THE PANEL
The retrieved evidence supports the PANEL-PROTOCOL's answer of BIOPSY, as the registrar found that the PI-RADS 4 score mandates biopsy according to the EAU guideline, and the previous notes confirmed "None" prior biopsy status.

THE OPEN QUESTIONS, ONE BY ONE
Q1. What is the significance of the PSA velocity (0.35 ng/mL/yr) in the context of the EAU guidelines for this decision? The retrieved documents indicate the PSA velocity shows fluctuation, which may not be a strong indicator on its own, but the PI-RADS 4 score is the primary driver according to the EAU guideline.

WHAT CARRIES WEIGHT, AND WHY
The PI-RADS 4 score is the most critical variable because the EAU guideline explicitly states that a PI-RADS score of $\ge 3$ triggers a biopsy. The prior biopsy status being "None" further supports proceeding with investigation.

MY SUGGESTION TO THE CHAIR
I suggest proceeding with a biopsy based on the PI-RADS 4 score and the lack of prior biopsy, as this aligns with the PANEL-PROTOCOL's conclusion.

VERDICT: ready | SUGGEST: biopsy | MISSING: none
